docs.text: Simple Stretch A small Android app that reminds you to stretch during the day, on your own schedule. Features Stretch library ("My stretches" in the home screen's menu): add, edit and delete stretches (name, instructions, optional duration). Ten common stretches are added on first run. You can also create a stretch straight from the goals screen and the reminder-time picker with "New stretch…". Schedules : as many as you like, each with a name, an on/off switch and the days of the week it runs. A schedule either has set times , each optionally with its own stretches (e.g. neck rolls at 10:00, hip flexors at 14:00), or repeats : every N minutes at a minute past the hour between two times, e.g. every hour at :50 from 8:00 to 17:00 (8:50 ... 16:50; the end time is inclusive). Daily goals : e.g. 3 hamstring stretches and 3 calf stretches a day, set with a − / + stepper next to every stretch on the goals screen (0 means no goal). The home screen shows today's progress ("Hamstring stretch 2/3"). Once every goal for the day is met, reminders stay quiet for the rest of the day. Trends ("Trends" in the home screen's menu, or on the goals card): a week or month bar chart of each day's score (goal stretches done, up to each target, out of the day's total target), the period's average, how many days met every goal, and your current streak. Tap a day to see its goals, the score climbing through the day, and every stretch logged with its time. Skipped days and days without goals are gaps, not 0%; changing a goal never rewrites past days. Home screen widget ("Today's goals", 2×2, resizable): a ring with one arc per daily goal, each filling as you do that stretch, around the app's stretch figure and today's count (a check mark once every goal is met). It follows light/dark mode and your wallpaper colours, starts again at 0 at midnight, and opens the app when tapped. Stretch sessions : from a reminder or the home screen's Stretch now , tick the stretches you did and save. Opened from a reminder, that reminder's stretches lead in their own section; otherwise stretches still short of today's goal do. Everything else follows alphabetically, and nothing is pre-checked. Skip a day : one tap on "Skip today", at the right of the home screen's "Today" heading (or in the top bar's menu), silences every reminder for the rest of the day; "Resume today" undoes it. Future days can be skipped from the calendar screen, and skipped days can be removed again. Notifications show the stretches (or today's unmet goals), with Start (opens the stretch session) and Snooze 5 min buttons; swipe to dismiss just this one. Tapping also opens the session. Reminders survive reboots and time or time-zone changes, and use exact alarms when Android allows them (falling back to slightly-less-punctual alarms when it doesn't). Behaviour is set out in the specification . Requirements Android 8.0 (API 26) or later. To build: JDK 17+, Android SDK with platform 36 and build-tools 36.0.0 (set ANDROID_HOME or sdk.dir in local.properties ). Build and install ./gradlew test # unit tests ./gradlew assembleDebug # app/build/outputs/apk/debug/simple-stretch-<version>-debug.apk adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/simple-stretch-*-debug.apk Or copy the APK to the phone and open it (allow installs from that source when asked). Application ID: from 0.3.0 the application ID is io.github.derekwinters.simple_stretch_android . An install of 0.1.0 or 0.2.0 ( com.derekwinters.stretch ) is a separate app: it will not update to new builds and keeps its own data until uninstalled. Nothing is carried over, so the new app starts empty, and the old one can be uninstalled whenever you like. Every pull request's CI run also uploads its debug APK as the simple-stretch-debug-apk workflow artifact (kept for 14 days). Pull requests from branches of this repository also upload simple-stretch-release-apk , signed with the release key, which installs in place over a release of 0.3.0 or later, so a PR can be tried before it is released without losing data. A debug APK and a release-signed APK cannot be installed over each other. Those pull requests also upload simple-stretch-release-aab , the release Android App Bundle signed with the same key; the AAB is the upload format for Google Play and cannot be installed directly, so sideload the APK. On first launch, allow notifications. On Android 12/12L, also allow "Alarms & reminders" if the app shows the banner, so reminders arrive on the minute. Store listing The Google Play screenshots are rendered from the app's screens on the JVM, not captured on a phone ( store listing specification ), and committed under fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/ ; their captions are in store/captions.md . The store icon ( images/icon.png , drawn from the app's launcher icon) and the feature graphic ( images/featureGraphic.png : a headline, whose text is also in captions.md , beside the Home and stretch session screens on two tilted phones) are rendered and checked the same way, by the same commands. ./gradlew verifyRoborazziDebug # compare with the committed store images (what CI runs) ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug # re-record them, deliberately, after changing a screen, caption or the launcher icon Every pull request's CI run verifies them; a changed or missing image fails the run and uploads the new and diff images as the store-screenshot-diffs workflow artifact. That run never records them. To re-record, either: apply the record-store-screenshots label to the pull request. CI records the images and pushes them as one commit to the branch store-screenshots/pr-<number> (never to the pull request's branch), says so in its job summary and removes the label. Bring that commit in with your own push ( git fetch origin store-screenshots/pr-<number> && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD ), so the pull request's CI run verifies it; or run ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug locally, on Linux with JDK 17 as CI runs, and commit the images. Either way the new images are reviewed in the pull request's diff. The listing's text (title, short description and full description) is written by hand in store/listing.md , one claim per line, each citing the requirement IDs it rests on. After editing it, compile it into fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/ and commit the result: python3 .github/scripts/store_listing.py # write title.txt, short_description.txt, full_description.txt python3 .github/scripts/store_listing.py --check # what CI runs; writes nothing Every pull request's CI run fails when a claim cites a missing or retired requirement, a headline feature page (marked <!-- store: headline --> ) has no claim, a text is over Google Play's limit, or the committed files differ from the listing. Releases Merging to main runs release-please, which keeps a release PR up to date from Conventional Commit titles. Merging that PR tags a release and attaches three files: simple-stretch-<version>-release.apk , for installing directly onto a phone (sideloading); simple-stretch-<version>-release.aab , the Android App Bundle for uploading to Google Play; store-listing-<version>.zip , the reviewed Google Play listing (text, screenshots, store icon and feature graphic) as committed at the release, under fastlane/metadata/android/ . The release only checks and packages it; it never writes listing text. Both are signed with a stable release key ( ADR 0002 ) and checked by the same signature gate before they are attached, so each release from 0.3.0 on upgrades the installed app in place and keeps its data. The same key is Google Play's app signing key ( ADR 0004 ), so an install from Google Play and a sideloaded release APK share one signature and can update each other in place to the same or a newer version. Each release's version code is derived from its version (0.3.0 is 300; see ADR 0003 ), so it rises with every release, as Google Play and Android require. Before a release is attached, a guard checks that its code is higher than the previous release's. The same check runs on the open release PR after every merge to main : a release PR whose code is not higher than the last release's gets a failing release-version-code status. One-time step: builds made before release signing (debug-signed releases, CI or local debug APKs) use a different key. Uninstall those once before installing the first release-signed build; after that, upgrades are in place. The same applies to moving from the old application ID: 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 ( com.derekwinters.stretch ) do not upgrade to 0.3.0 or later, which install alongside them as a new, empty app; uninstall the old one when you no longer need it. Project layout app/src/main/java/com/derekwinters/stretch/ data/ Room entities, DAOs, database (+ seed, migrations), repository goals/ goal progress, goal history and session ordering maths (pure Kotlin) trends/ daily score, periods, streak and intraday series maths (pure Kotlin) scheduling/ next-occurrence and repeating-slot maths, AlarmManager scheduling, snooze, alarm + reschedule receivers notifications/ notification channel/content and the Snooze / Skip actions widget/ segmented ring home screen widget: ring layout and palette (pure Kotlin), bitmap renderer, provider and redraws ui/ Compose screens: home, schedule editor, stretch session, goals, trends (Canvas charts) and day detail, stretch library, skipped days app/src/test/ JVM unit tests (next occurrence, repeating slots, goal maths, goal history, trends, widget ring and palette) and the store image tests (store/) app/schemas/ exported Room schemas docs/spec/ requirements with IDs; docs/adr/ decisions; docs/store/ listing text and screenshot captions fastlane/ Google Play listing text (compiled from docs/store/listing.md) and images Notes Exact reminders need the user-granted SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM ("Alarms & reminders") on Android 12 and later. On Android 14 and later it starts denied on a new install, so reminders are inexact (may arrive a few minutes late) until the user taps Allow on the home-screen banner. USE_EXACT_ALARM is deliberately not declared: Google Play restricts it to alarm, timer and calendar apps. Some manufacturers aggressively stop background apps; if reminders go missing, exempt the app from battery optimisation.

docs.text: Privacy policy Effective date: 27 October 2026 Simple Stretch stores what you enter on your phone and never goes online, so it sends nothing anywhere itself. It has no accounts, no analytics and no ads, and it does not ask for internet permission. Nothing is collected by, or shared with, the developer. What the app stores The app stores the following, on your device only: the stretches in your library (name, instructions and optional duration); your schedules and their reminder times (days of the week, set times or repeating windows, and which stretches each reminder prompts); your daily goals and their history (each goal count and the days it applied); the stretches you log, each with the time you logged it; the days you chose to skip; the scheduler's own settings: when each reminder alarm is next due and when the last reminder was shown, so a reminder is not shown twice. This data stays in the app's private storage on your phone. Android keeps it private to the app; other apps on the phone do not have access to it. (Android's device backup, below, is a separate copy.) What the app does not do It has no internet permission, so it does not send anything anywhere itself. It has no accounts or sign-in. It contains no analytics, advertising, crash reporting or other third-party software development kits (SDKs). Nothing is collected by, or shared with, the developer or anyone else. Permissions The app asks Android for three permissions, and uses them only for reminders: Notifications : to show your stretch reminders. Alarms and reminders : to show each reminder at the time you set. Without it, Android may deliver reminders a little late. Run at startup : to set your reminders again after the phone restarts. Device backup The app allows Android's own device backup and sets no limits on it, so all of the app's data is included. If backup is turned on in your phone's settings, Android may copy all of the app's data to your Google account and restore it later. When you move to a new phone, Android can also copy it directly from the old phone to the new one. That backup and transfer are handled by Android and Google under your Google account's settings, not by the developer, who has no access to it. Deleting your data To delete everything the app has stored, clear its storage (in Android's settings, open Apps, choose Stretch, then Storage, then Clear storage; the exact names vary between phones) or uninstall the app. A copy in your Google account's device backup is managed in your Google account. Children The app is not directed at children under 13. Changes to this policy Changes to this policy are made in the app's public repository, and the effective date above changes with them. The history of every change is kept there. Contact Questions or concerns: open an issue at https://github.com/derekwinters/simple-stretch-android/issues . Play data safety form The answers to give in Google Play Console's data safety form: Question Answer Does your app collect or share any of the required user data types? No (assumption below). Is all of the user data collected by your app encrypted in transit? Not shown: Play asks this only when the first answer is "Yes". Do you provide a way for users to request that their data is deleted? Not shown: Play asks this only when the first answer is "Yes". Data types collected None (assumption below). Data types shared None (assumption below). Basis: Play Console Help, "Provide information for Google Play's Data safety section" ( https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469 ), defines "collect" as transmitting data from your app off a user's device, and says user data processed only locally on the device need not be disclosed. That page does not mention Android Auto Backup or device-to-device transfer. The "No" and "None" answers therefore rest on an assumption: that Android's own Auto Backup and device-to-device transfer, system services run by Android and Google under the user's account rather than transmission by the app, are not "collection" by the app. The page does not confirm this, and the owner must confirm it before entering these answers in Play Console. If the assumption is wrong, the answers change: the first answer becomes "Yes", the stored data types are listed as collected, and the deletion answer becomes "Yes: clear the app's storage or uninstall".

docs.text: 0001: Debug-sign release builds until a release keystore exists Status: superseded by 0002 Superseded. Release builds are now signed with the stable release keystore; see ADR 0002 . This record is kept for history. The release build type uses signingConfig = signingConfigs.debug , and the release-please workflow builds and attaches that APK to each GitHub Release without referencing any secrets. There is no release keystore yet, and no Play Store listing to install against. Setting up key custody (where the keystore lives, who can read it, how it is rotated) has no payoff until the app is published somewhere that needs a stable signing identity, so it is deferred. Consequences Release APKs are debug-signed. CI runners each generate their own debug key, so two releases may be signed by different keys: updating in place can fail with INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE , and the fix is to uninstall and reinstall (which clears the app's schedules and skipped days). When a stable keystore is introduced, a new ADR supersedes this one; the release build type then reads the keystore from environment variables (never a committed file), as the sibling Android repos do, and every existing install needs one uninstall/reinstall.

docs.text: 0002: Sign release builds with a stable release keystore Status: accepted (supersedes 0001 ); partially superseded by 0004 Partially superseded. The app is now also published on Google Play, with this release key enrolled as both the Play app signing key and the upload key; see ADR 0004 . The statements below that the app is sideloaded with no Play App Signing or key recovery, and that the Play key choice is open, are replaced by it. The rest of this record stands. docs.text: 0003: Derive the version code from the version name Status: accepted Context Android and Google Play order builds by versionCode , an integer, not by the version name. Play rejects an upload whose versionCode it has already seen for the app, and will not offer a build with a lower code than the installed one as an update; a device refuses to install such an update too. Until now the code was a hand-set VERSION_CODE=1 in gradle.properties that nothing bumped: releases 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 both shipped as code 1, and the second Play upload would have been refused. The guard below requires each release's code to be strictly higher than the previous release's, which satisfies all of these. release-please already owns the version name ( VERSION_NAME in gradle.properties , rewritten from Conventional Commit titles). A second number kept in step by hand is a number that drifts. Decision The version code is computed from VERSION_NAME at build time; there is no VERSION_CODE property. versionCode = major * 10000 + minor * 100 + patch Version Code 0.2.0 200 0.3.0 300 (the first release under this scheme; 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 were code 1) 0.99.99 9999 1.0.0 10000 The conversion lives in buildSrc/ ( VersionCode.fromVersionName ) and is unit-tested there; app/build.gradle.kts sets defaultConfig.versionCode from it, so debug and release builds of one version share one code. It accepts only MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH , three dot-separated numbers without leading zeros ( 0.03.0 is refused): no v prefix, no pre-release or build suffix. Minor and patch are capped at 99 , and the code may not exceed 2100000000, Google Play's largest allowed versionCode . Anything else fails the build with a message naming the value. Invariant — the conversion never wraps, clamps or truncates. A version it cannot represent fails the build; it never produces some other, smaller code. Under the caps the scheme is strictly increasing: a higher version always has a higher code, including across a carry (0.2.99 → 299 < 0.3.0 → 300; 0.99.99 → 9999 < 1.0.0 → 10000). Escape hatch. If a minor or patch ever needs to pass 99, switch to major * 1000000 + minor * 1000 + patch (caps 999). That switch is always safe: for every version the new code is at least the old one (with minor and patch at most 99, the difference is major * 990000 + minor * 900 ), so the first build under it is higher than every earlier release. Switching the other way is never safe. Release guard .github/scripts/check_version_code.py refuses a release whose code is not strictly higher than the previous release's. The previous release is the newest GitHub release by publish time that is neither a draft nor a pre-release, leaving out the tag being released. It is the newest by publish time, not the one with the highest code. It downloads that release's simple-stretch-*-release.apk with gh release download <tag> --pattern 'simple-stretch-*-release.apk' and reads both codes with aapt2 dump badging . Invariant — the new code is read from the APK that was actually built, never recomputed from the formula , so a build that ignores the formula is still caught. It passes only when the new code is strictly greater; otherwise it fails, naming both codes and both versions. Edge cases: no published release at all: passes with a notice (nothing to compare against); the previous release has no matching APK, or more than one: fails, naming the tag, and points to the backfill_tag input of the release-please workflow, which re-attaches it; the listing, download or aapt2 fails, or aapt2 prints output the parser does not recognise: fails (it never passes on a reading it is unsure of); a manual backfill ( workflow_dispatch with backfill_tag ) of the newest published release is guarded exactly like a release ( --backfill-tag decides this with the same release selection, then compares against the release before it), so re-attaching cannot bypass a guard that failed on release. Only a backfill of an older release skips the guard, with a notice: it is lower than newer releases by design. On release: the build-and-attach job of release-please.yml runs the guard on the signed release APK after the signature gate and before the attach step, from the main checkout like the signature gate. Invariant — a release, or a backfill of the newest release, whose APK's code is not higher than the previous release's gets no APK or AAB attached. The guard reads only the APK. The AAB is covered only because the APK and the AAB come out of one Gradle invocation ( assembleRelease bundleRelease ) with one versionCode . Invariant — the release APK and AAB are built in the same Gradle invocation; splitting the AAB build into a separate step or job leaves it unchecked by this guard, and would need the guard run on the AAB as well. On the release PR: the release-pr-guard job runs on every push to main after release-please has updated its PR. When a release PR is open it checks out the PR's head, builds the debug APK (same derived code), runs the guard and posts a commit status named release-version-code on the PR's head commit: success , or failure with the reason. A release PR that would publish a lower or equal code is visible before it is merged. Consequences Google Play's own record is the authority, and the guard cannot see it. It compares against the previous GitHub release's APK only. A build uploaded to Play by hand, outside a GitHub release, is invisible to it, and a later release could pass the guard yet still be refused by Play. Checking Play itself needs a Play Developer API credential, which is part of automated upload (#26). Until then, every Play upload should be a GitHub release asset. 0.3.0 (code 300) is the first code above the 1 that v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 shipped with. The jump from 1 to 300 is intentional and permanent: codes never go back down. Minor and patch stop at 99 until the escape hatch is taken; the build says so rather than publishing a wrong code. Pre-release versions ( 0.3.0-beta ) cannot be built; release-please is configured for plain releases only. The formula tests are not part of ./gradlew test : buildSrc is a separate build whose tests Gradle does not run for the main build. They run with ./gradlew -p buildSrc test , which pr.yml runs on every pull request.

docs.text: 0004: Enrol the release key as the Play app signing key Status: accepted (partially supersedes 0002 ) Context Simple Stretch is going on Google Play as well as being released on GitHub. New apps on Play use Play App Signing: the developer uploads an Android App Bundle signed with an upload key , and Google re-signs the APKs it delivers with the app signing key it holds. What a phone sees is the app signing key, so that is the key every later update, from any source, must match. ADR 0002 was written for a sideloaded app with no Play App Signing. Its stable release keystore already signs both the release APK attached to each GitHub Release and the release AAB beside it (#40, #73). The open question was how that key relates to the two keys Play needs, and it has to be settled before the first Play release, because the app signing key cannot be swapped afterwards without breaking updates for everyone who installed from Play. Two questions were decided: (1) which key Play signs installs with, and (2) whether GitHub Releases keep the APK. Options considered: 1A. Upload the existing release key as the app signing key, and keep it as the upload key. Play installs and GitHub-released APKs then carry one signature. 1B. Keep the existing key as the app signing key, with a separate upload key. A leaked upload key can be reset through Play, but CI would sign the AAB with a second keystore and a second set of secrets, while the APK keeps the first: two keys to hold and never lose instead of one, for protection that only covers uploads. 1C. Let Google generate the app signing key. Google holds the only copy, so the sideloaded APK could never be signed with it: a Play install and a GitHub-released APK could not update each other, and moving between them would mean uninstalling and losing the app's data. 2. Keep or drop the GitHub-released APK. Dropping it would make Play the only install path; keeping it serves people without Play and costs nothing under 1A, since it is signed with the same key. Decision Option 1A. The stable release keystore of ADR 0002 is uploaded to Play Console as the app signing key, and the same key stays the upload key. Users who install from Play and users who install the APK from a GitHub Release run builds signed by the same certificate, so either can update the other in place to the same or a newer version, keeping its data. CI keeps signing the release AAB with the current secrets. The AAB build, the signature gate and the secrets of ADR 0002 need no change. GitHub Releases keep attaching the release-signed APK next to the AAB, for people who do not use Play. Enrolling the key in Play App Signing is done in Play Console by the owner (#48), following this record. What this supersedes in ADR 0002 Only ADR 0002's statements that Simple Stretch is sideloaded with no Play App Signing and no key recovery, and its consequence that leaves the choice between app signing key and upload key open. The rest of ADR 0002 stands: the one stable keystore, its secrets, the unsigned-never-debug-signed invariant, and the signature gate on every APK and AAB. Consequences One key both uploads and signs what users install. If it leaks, the key every install trusts is exposed, not only the upload path. It stays only in repository secrets and with the owner. If it leaks, register a new upload key through Play at once; installs keep trusting the leaked key. The key must never change , as in ADR 0002, now for Play installs as well as sideloaded ones. The choice cannot be undone after the first Play release. Once Play has delivered builds signed with this key, the app signing key is fixed for everyone who installed them. If the key is lost, Play can register a new upload key, and Play releases continue under the app signing key Google holds. GitHub-released APKs could then no longer be signed with the matching key, so sideloaded installs would have to uninstall once to move to a new key, and could no longer update to or from Play installs.

docs.text: Goals GOAL-001 A goal says how many times a day the user wants to do one stretch, e.g. 3 hamstring stretches a day. It has a stretch and a count of 1 to 20. A stretch has at most one current goal (GOAL-008). The goals screen's stepper runs from 0 to 20: 0 is shown for a stretch with no goal and is never stored as a goal. GOAL-002 The goals screen lists every stretch in the library, in library order (by name, ignoring case, as "My stretches" does), under a short intro line. Each row has the stretch's name, " n of count today" when it has a goal (with a ✓ once the goal is met, GOAL-003), and a − N + stepper showing its current goal, 0 when it has none. + on 0 adds a goal of 1; + or − on 1 to 20 changes the count by one; − on 1 removes the goal (GOAL-006). − is disabled at 0 and + at 20. Each tap is applied at once through GOAL-009; there is no Save step and no dialog. "New stretch…" at the bottom of the list opens the stretch editor (LIB-007); the new stretch then appears in the list at 0. It is reached from the home screen's top bar and its goals card (HOME-004, HOME-006). Invariant — A tap is one GOAL-009 edit. Each stepper tap runs exactly one setGoal or removeGoal , in one transaction. Repeated taps on the same day update today's row in place and never leave one-day history rows; the screen never writes goal history of its own. Invariant — The goals screen uses only the theme's colour roles. A stepper with a goal uses primaryContainer / onPrimaryContainer (as the "New schedule" button); a stepper at 0 uses surfaceContainerHighest (as the "Today's goals" card), with − in the disabled content colour. The ✓ and "New stretch…" use primary (as "Edit goals"). There are no Color(…) literals, so the screen follows dynamic colour and dark mode like the rest of the app. - GOAL-003 A goal's progress on a day is the number of completions of its stretch (SESS-004) whose time falls within that local calendar day, from midnight inclusive to the next midnight exclusive. A goal is met when progress is at or above the count; progress above the count is shown as is (e.g. 4/3). - GOAL-004 Invariant — Progress is always derived from the completion log, never stored. There is no counter to reset: a new day starts at 0 because no completions fall in it yet, and changing or removing a goal never changes the history. - GOAL-005 Once every goal for the day is met, reminders are not shown for the rest of that day (NOTIF-010); the schedule keeps running and reminders return the next day, or as soon as a goal is short again (e.g. after a goal's count is raised). With no goals, goals never suppress a reminder. Goals also decide what the session suggests (SESS-002) and what a reminder without stretches lists (NOTIF-001). - GOAL-006 Removing a goal keeps its stretch's completion history. Deleting the stretch removes both (LIB-005). - GOAL-007 Invariant — Upgrading the app never loses data. The database moves from version 1 to 2 with an explicit migration: it adds the repeating-schedule columns to schedules with defaults that keep every existing schedule a set-times schedule, and creates the goals and completions tables. Version 2 to 3 is GOAL-010. There is no destructive-migration fallback. Goal history GOAL-008 Goals are versioned so trends can judge each day by the goals of that day (TREND-001). Each goal row has a stretch, a count, a first day in force ( effectiveFromEpochDay , inclusive) and an optional end day ( effectiveToEpochDay , exclusive). The row with no end day is the stretch's current goal ; every screen other than trends, and notifications, use current goals only. GOAL-009 Editing and removing goals, on day T (today): adding a goal to a stretch without one adds a current row from T ; changing the count of a current goal that started before T closes it with end T and adds a new current row from T with the new count, so the new count applies from today and earlier days keep the old one; changing the count of a current goal that started on T updates it in place (no one-day history rows); setting the same count changes nothing; removing a current goal that started before T closes it with end T (today is judged without it); removing one that started on T deletes it. Invariant — A stretch has at most one current goal, and history rows are only ever closed, never rewritten. Each change runs in one transaction that reads the current row and applies exactly one of the edits above; nothing changes a closed row's count or range. Deleting the stretch deletes all its goal rows (LIB-005). - GOAL-010 Invariant — Upgrading to version 3 keeps every goal. The migration rebuilds goals with the two new columns (SQLite cannot add a NOT NULL column without a default or turn the old unique index on stretchId into a plain one): each existing goal keeps its id, stretch and count, becomes a current goal (no end day), and is in force from the local date of the earliest completion in the log , or from the day of the upgrade if nothing was logged yet. Version 2 created goals and completions together, so goals were in use from about the first completion; starting there shows those days in trends, while starting from the epoch would invent months of 0% days before the app was used. Build checklist [x] GoalMath (progress, day bounds, session layout, notification summary) is pure and unit tested (GOAL-003, SESS-002, NOTIF-001). [x] goals.stretchId has an index and a cascading foreign key (GOAL-001, LIB-005); since version 3 it is not unique, as a stretch has history rows (GOAL-008). [x] MIGRATION_1_2 SQL matches the entities, including @ColumnInfo(defaultValue) on the new schedules columns, so Room's schema validation passes (GOAL-007). [x] GoalMath.allGoalsMet is false for an empty goal list (GOAL-005, NOTIF-010). [x] GoalHistory.planSet / planRemove / migratedStartDay are pure and unit tested (GOAL-009, GOAL-010). [x] GoalDao.setGoal / removeGoal are @Transaction methods that read the current row and apply one GoalEdit (GOAL-009 invariant). [x] MIGRATION_2_3 creates goals_new with Room's exact v3 DDL (column order, nullability, foreign key, then the plain index_goals_stretchId ), copies ids, drops and renames (GOAL-010). [x] Count is clamped to at least 1 in the repository, not only in the UI (GOAL-001). [x] GoalStepper.plan maps a tap to one edit (add, change, remove or nothing) and keeps the stepper within 0 to 20; it is pure and unit tested (GOAL-001, GOAL-002). [x] GoalMath.goalRows lists every stretch by name with its count (0 without a goal) and today's progress; it is pure and unit tested (GOAL-002). [x] Each stepper tap calls exactly one repository setGoal / removeGoal ; same-day taps leave one current row and no history rows (GOAL-002 invariant, GOAL-009). [x] GoalsScreen.kt has no Color( literal; its colours are the MaterialTheme.colorScheme roles named in GOAL-002. [ ] Instrumented migration tests (1→2, 2→3) with MigrationTestHelper (need an emulator and the committed 1.json / 2.json schemas). [x] Store listing reviewed: every claim in docs/store/listing.md that cites this page is still true, and at least one does ( store: headline ; STORE-LIST-003, STORE-LIST-004).

docs.text: Stretch library LIB-001 The user can add, edit and delete stretches. A stretch has a name, optional instructions, and an optional duration in seconds. LIB-002 On first run the library is seeded with common stretches (neck rolls, shoulder shrugs, chest opener, hamstring, hip flexor, wrist, upper back, quad, spinal twist, calf). Invariant — Seeding never re-adds a stretch the user deleted. It runs only when the database is first created, never on later launches. - LIB-003 Deleting a stretch removes it from any reminder times that use it; the reminder times themselves remain. - LIB-004 Editing a stretch changes what future notifications say; it does not change any schedule's timing. - LIB-005 Deleting a stretch also deletes its goal (GOAL-001) and its completion history (SESS-004). - LIB-006 The library screen is titled "My stretches". It shows a hint at the top, "Add your own stretches with +", above the list, and its + button opens the stretch editor for a new stretch. - LIB-007 "New stretch…" is offered in two places: the goals screen's "New stretch…" link (GOAL-002) and a set-times reminder's stretch picker in the schedule editor (SCHED-002). It opens the same stretch editor the library uses (name, optional instructions, optional duration). From the schedule editor, saving adds the stretch to the library and selects it in the picker; cancelling returns to the picker unchanged. From the goals screen, saving adds the stretch and it appears in the goals list at 0; cancelling changes nothing. Invariant — A stretch created from a picker is a normal library stretch , saved at once whether or not the picker is then confirmed, and the picker keeps the selections the user had already made. Build checklist [x] Seed lives in RoomDatabase.Callback.onCreate (LIB-002 invariant). [x] Cross-reference table cascades on stretch delete (LIB-003). [x] goals and completions foreign keys cascade on stretch delete (LIB-005). [x] One shared StretchEditDialog composable serves the library, the goals screen and the schedule picker (LIB-007). [x] The repository's insert returns the new id so the picker can select it (LIB-007). [x] Store listing reviewed: this page is store: omit , and any claim in docs/store/listing.md that cites it is still true (STORE-LIST-002, STORE-LIST-003).

docs.text: Notifications NOTIF-001 A reminder notification's title is the stretch name(s); its expanded text lists each stretch with its duration and instructions. The schedule name is shown as the sub-text. A reminder with no stretches (every repeating schedule, SCHED-011) is titled "Time to stretch"; its text lists today's goals that are still short, as "Hamstring stretch 1 of 3", or (with no goals) shows the generic message. (Once every goal is met no reminder is shown at all, NOTIF-010.) NOTIF-002 Tapping the notification opens the stretch session screen (SESS-001) and dismisses the notification. It carries the reminder's named stretches, its schedule name and its scheduled time into the session, which lists those stretches as their own section (SESS-002). A reminder with no stretches carries no named list. NOTIF-003 A "Start" action does the same as tapping: it opens the stretch session screen with the same named stretches, schedule name and scheduled time, and dismisses the notification. (It replaces the earlier "Done" action.) NOTIF-004 Retired. It described a "Skip today" notification action, which was removed. Skipping today is done from the home screen (SKIP-001) or the "Skipped days" screen (SKIP-002). A notification posted before the removal may still show the old button; tapping it does nothing (no skip is written and the notification is not dismissed), and the notification stays until swiped away or replaced. NOTIF-005 On Android 13+ the app asks for POST_NOTIFICATIONS on first launch. While notifications are blocked, the home screen shows a banner linking to the app's notification settings. NOTIF-006 An occurrence delivered more than 2 hours late (e.g. held by Doze) is not shown. NOTIF-007 Invariant — One occurrence produces at most one notification. If the same occurrence is delivered twice (a reschedule re-armed it, SCHED-008), the second delivery is ignored. NOTIF-008 A "Snooze 5 min" action dismisses the notification and posts the same reminder again 5 minutes later (SCHED-015). Snoozing again from the re-posted notification snoozes again. Invariant — A snooze keeps the original scheduled time. The re-posted reminder (and any snooze of it) carries the time it was first scheduled for, so the session heading says "From your 9:00 … reminder" even when it was re-posted at 9:05 (SESS-002). NOTIF-009 Dismissing just this reminder is done by swiping the notification away (it is not ongoing). A reminder shows exactly two action buttons, Start and Snooze 5 min, in that order; the third slot Android allows is left empty. Invariant — No notification button skips a day. The reminder carries no skip action, and NotificationActionReceiver handles only Snooze; any other action it receives, including the old Skip today action, writes nothing and leaves the notification alone. - NOTIF-010 When at least one goal exists and every goal's progress today (GOAL-003) is at or above its count, a reminder is not shown. This applies to every reminder: set times (with or without stretches), repeating schedules and snoozed reminders. It is decided when the alarm is delivered, from the completion log at that moment, after the NOTIF-007 duplicate check and the enabled, day, skip and staleness checks. With no goals, reminders are shown as before. Invariant — Met goals suppress the notification, never the schedule. The next alarm is still armed exactly as if the reminder had been shown (SCHED-006), so logging one more stretch, or a new day starting, never needs a reschedule for reminders to resume. With no goals defined, goals never suppress anything. Build checklist [x] Channel created at app start with high importance. [x] All PendingIntents are FLAG_IMMUTABLE . [x] Receiver remembers the last-notified trigger per reminder (NOTIF-007). [x] Start and the content tap share one activity PendingIntent carrying the notification id; MainActivity cancels that notification and navigates to the session (NOTIF-002/003). [x] Snooze is a broadcast action handled by NotificationActionReceiver (NOTIF-008). [x] The scheduled time travels notification → snooze alarm → re-posted notification as an extra; only a missing extra (an alarm armed before this) falls back to the trigger time (NOTIF-008 invariant). [x] The reminder's buttons come from one pure list, unit tested as exactly Start then Snooze; the receiver's handled actions are a pure set, unit tested to exclude the old Skip today action (NOTIF-004 retired, NOTIF-009). [x] "Every goal met" is the pure GoalMath.allGoalsMet (false for no goals), unit tested (NOTIF-010). [x] The receiver returns before posting, but onAlarmHandled still runs, so the next alarm is armed (NOTIF-010 invariant). [ ] Robolectric test for notification content (not yet). [x] Store listing reviewed: this page is store: omit , and any claim in docs/store/listing.md that cites it is still true (STORE-LIST-002, STORE-LIST-003).

docs.text: Scheduling SCHED-001 The user can create any number of schedules. Each schedule has a name, an enabled toggle, a set of days of the week (picked with chips), and a mode: set times (a list of reminder times) or repeating (SCHED-011). SCHED-002 In a set-times schedule each reminder time has its own set of stretches (zero or more; picking stretches is optional, and the picker can create a new stretch, LIB-007). A time with no stretches still reminds, with a generic "Time to stretch" message and today's unmet goals (NOTIF-001). SCHED-003 A reminder's next occurrence is the first date-time strictly after now , at the reminder's time, on a day the schedule selects, and not on a skipped date (SKIP-004). Invariant — A reminder never fires on a day its schedule does not select. This is checked twice: when the alarm is computed, and again by the receiver when the alarm is delivered. - SCHED-004 A disabled schedule, or one with no days selected, has no alarms set. - SCHED-005 Each reminder time, and each repeating schedule, has at most one alarm. Its alarm key is the reminder's id for a reminder time and the negated schedule id for a repeating schedule (ids start at 1, so the two never collide). The key is the PendingIntent request code and the notification id. Setting an alarm again replaces the previous one; alarms of keys that no longer exist are cancelled. - SCHED-006 All alarms are recomputed after every alarm is handled, after every data change (schedule saved, deleted or toggled; date skipped or un-skipped), when the app starts, and on BOOT_COMPLETED , TIME_SET , TIMEZONE_CHANGED , MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED and SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM_PERMISSION_STATE_CHANGED . - SCHED-007 Alarms are exact ( setExactAndAllowWhileIdle ) when the app may schedule exact alarms. SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is the only exact-alarm permission the app declares, and on Android 12 and later it is granted by the user ("Alarms & reminders" in system settings); on Android 14 and later a new install starts with it denied; below Android 12 (API 26 to 30) exact alarms need no permission. USE_EXACT_ALARM is deliberately not declared: Google Play restricts it to alarm, timer and calendar apps, and the user cannot revoke it. Without the grant, alarms fall back to setAndAllowWhileIdle , and the home screen shows a banner linking to the system setting (HOME-005). Invariant — Losing the exact-alarm permission degrades timing, never delivery. A refused exact alarm is always replaced by an inexact one, never dropped. - SCHED-008 An alarm whose time has passed but which has not yet been handled (possible with inexact alarms) is kept for up to 30 minutes by any reschedule, rather than being moved to the next day. Invariant — A reschedule never silently drops an occurrence that was due and not yet delivered. - SCHED-009 Reminder times have minute precision; seconds are ignored. - SCHED-010 Times are local wall-clock times: 10:00 stays 10:00 after a time-zone or daylight-saving change. Invariant — The app's clock reports the device's default zone at the moment it is asked, never a zone saved earlier. A clock built once at process start must not hold on to the zone it was built with (SCHED-016). Repeating schedules SCHED-011 A repeating schedule has a start time S , an end time E , an interval of N minutes (5 to 720, default 60) and a minute past the hour M (0 to 59, default 0). It has no per-time stretches; the stretch session suggests stretches from goals instead (SESS-002). SCHED-012 A repeating schedule's slots on a day are: the first time at or after S whose minute is M , then every N minutes after it, for as long as the slot is at or before E . The end time is inclusive: a slot exactly at E fires. Slots never cross midnight. If E is before S , or no slot fits, the schedule has no slots. Example: 08:00 to 17:00, every 60 minutes at :50 gives 08:50, 09:50, ... 16:50 (17:50 is past the end). 08:00 to 17:00 every 60 minutes at :00 gives 08:00 ... 17:00, including 17:00. With an interval that does not divide 60 the minute only anchors the first slot: 08:00 to 12:00 every 45 minutes at :10 gives 08:10, 08:55, 09:40, 10:25, 11:10, 11:55. - SCHED-013 A repeating schedule's next occurrence is the first slot strictly after now , on a day the schedule selects and not on a skipped date. The SCHED-003 invariant applies: the receiver re-checks the day, the skip list and that the schedule is still enabled and repeating before notifying. - SCHED-014 Saving a schedule as repeating removes its set reminder times (and their stretch choices); saving a set-times schedule ignores the repeating fields. Every timing change reschedules (SCHED-006). Snooze SCHED-015 Snoozing a reminder (NOTIF-008) sets a one-shot alarm 5 minutes later that posts the same reminder again. It is a separate alarm (its own intent action) and is not remembered by the scheduler. Invariant — Snoozing never moves the schedule. The schedule's own next alarm stays where it was; a snooze is never written to the scheduler's remembered alarms and no reschedule cancels or replaces it. A snoozed reminder that comes due on a skipped date, or whose schedule was disabled or deleted, is not shown (SKIP-003). A pending snooze does not survive a reboot. Current time SCHED-016 The app reads the current date, time and time zone from one clock, created in StretchApp and handed to everything that needs it: screens, ViewModels, the repository, the scheduler, receivers, the widget and database migrations. Nothing else reads the system clock or the default zone. Tests and screenshot runs replace it with a fixed clock (instant and zone). docs.text: Screens HOME-001 The home screen shows today's date at the top. There is no skip card; skipping today is done from the Today row (HOME-002) or the overflow menu (HOME-004). HOME-002 Below it, today's reminders from all enabled schedules, in time order, with the time, stretches and schedule name. A repeating schedule shows as one row at its next slot today (or its last slot, dimmed, once all have passed) with its repeat summary and how many slots are left today. Reminders already past, or all of them when today is skipped, are dimmed. The "Today" heading row carries a text button at its right end (SKIP-001): "Skip today" while today is not skipped (enabled when at least one reminder is left today, shown disabled when none are), and "Resume today" once today is skipped. Every row opens the stretch session when tapped (HOME-009). Invariant — When today is skipped, the Today row always shows "Resume today". No state hides it: not an empty Today list, not the time of day, and nothing stored per device. - HOME-003 Below that, every schedule with its days, its times (or repeat summary, e.g. "Every 60 min at :50, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM") and an enabled switch. Tapping a schedule opens its editor; a button creates a new one. - HOME-004 The top bar has at most two icon actions plus an overflow menu. The goals screen is an icon ("Daily goals"); the overflow menu holds labelled text items "Skip today" (or "Resume today"), "Skip other days" (the skipped-days screen), "My stretches" (the stretch library, LIB-006) and "Trends" (TREND-004). The top bar's title is the app's name, "Simple Stretch", read from app_name (STORE-LIST-008). Invariant — The stretch library is reached by a labelled item , never only by an unlabelled icon. - HOME-005 Banners appear when notifications are blocked (NOTIF-005) or exact alarms are not allowed (SCHED-007). Invariant — Toggling a schedule's switch on the home screen reschedules immediately ; there is no separate save step for it. HOME-006 A "Today's goals" card, below the date, shows each goal's progress today (e.g. "Hamstring stretch 2/3" with a progress bar) and links to the goals screen and, in its header while goals exist, to the Trends screen (TREND-009). With no goals it invites the user to set one. HOME-007 A "Stretch now" button on the goals card opens the stretch session screen (SESS-001) without waiting for a reminder. HOME-008 Retired. It described the closable "Skip today" card, which was removed with its close (X) button and its stored closed date. Its invariant, a skipped day is never hidden, now lives in HOME-002. HOME-009 Tapping any row of the Today list (HOME-002) opens the stretch session screen (SESS-001) as that reminder's notification would (NOTIF-002). Every row is tappable: past, upcoming and current alike, and also while today is skipped. A set-time row opens the session with its reminder's named stretches, its schedule name and the row's time today; a repeating schedule's row, whose reminders name no stretches (SCHED-011), opens it with no named list ("Goals still short today"), as its notification does. docs.text: Stretch sessions SESS-001 The stretch session screen is where the user records what they stretched. It opens from a reminder notification (tap or "Start", NOTIF-002, NOTIF-003), from the "Stretch now" button on the home screen (HOME-007) and from a row of the home screen's Today list, which opens it as that reminder's notification would (HOME-009). A reminder opens it carrying the reminder's named stretches, its schedule name and its original scheduled time (NOTIF-002, NOTIF-008); "Stretch now" and a reminder with no stretches (every repeating schedule, SCHED-011) carry no named list. SESS-002 It lists every stretch in the library once, each with a checkbox and a progress label: "n of target today" for an unmet goal, "Goal met: n of target today" for a met one, "No goal" otherwise. The list has two sections: Top section, opened from a reminder that names stretches: headed "From your {time} {schedule} reminder" (e.g. "From your 9:00 Morning reminder"; the time in the user's 12/24 hour format), it lists that reminder's stretches in the order the reminder names them, on a highlighted background. A reminder stretch whose goal is already met stays here with its progress. A named stretch that no longer exists (deleted, LIB-003) is left out without any note; if none of the named stretches still exists, the screen opens as if with no named list. Top section, opened with no named list: headed "Goals still short today", it lists the stretches whose goal is not yet met today, by name ignoring case, on a highlighted background. It is left out when no goal is short (every goal met, or no goals at all). "Other stretches": every stretch not in the top section, by name ignoring case (ties by id), always expanded. With no top section the screen is just this alphabetical list. Invariant — Nothing is pre-checked. Every checkbox, in both sections, starts unchecked, whichever way the screen was opened, so only what the user taps is logged. - SESS-003 "Save" records one completion per checked stretch, in either section, all stamped with the moment of saving, then closes the screen. Save is disabled while nothing is checked in either section. Leaving the screen any other way records nothing. - SESS-004 The completion log stores, per completion, the stretch and the time it was completed (epoch milliseconds). Deleting a stretch deletes its completions (LIB-005). - SESS-005 Invariant — The list order is fixed when the screen opens. Both sections, and which stretch is in which, are decided once. Checking a box never moves a row, and progress changing in the background (e.g. a save from another screen) does not reorder the list while it is shown. Saving a session only appends to the completion log; it never changes schedules or alarms. Build checklist [x] Both sections are computed once by GoalMath.sessionLayout from a one-shot read (SESS-002, SESS-005); it is pure and unit tested, including deleted named stretches. [x] The reminder's stretch ids, schedule name and scheduled time travel as session route arguments, so they survive process death (SESS-001). [x] A Today row and a notification build the session route with one shared function (SESS-001, HOME-009). [x] The checked set starts empty for every way of opening (SESS-002 invariant). [x] All completions of one save are inserted in one transaction with one timestamp (SESS-003). [x] completions has indices on stretchId and completedAt (SESS-004, GOAL-003). docs.text: Skipping days SKIP-001 The "Today" heading row on the home screen has a "Skip today" text button at its right end (HOME-002). Pressing it suppresses every remaining reminder for today across all schedules. It is shown but disabled when no reminders are left today, and once today is skipped the same spot shows a "Resume today" text button that undoes the skip. SKIP-002 The user can skip any future date, picked with a date picker, from the "Skipped days" screen. That screen lists today and future skipped dates, each removable. SKIP-003 Invariant — A skipped date never produces a notification, even if an alarm for it was already scheduled. The alarm receiver checks the skip list for the occurrence's date before notifying; it does not rely on the alarm having been rescheduled. SKIP-004 When computing a reminder's next occurrence, skipped dates are passed over. SKIP-005 Retired. It described a "Skip today" action on every reminder notification, which was removed (NOTIF-004 retired, NOTIF-009). Skips are stored separately, per date, and apply to all schedules; the next scheduled day reminds as normal. SKIP-007 Past skipped dates are kept (they were pruned before version 3), because trends leave skipped days out (TREND-003). The skipped-days screen still lists only today and future dates. docs.text: Store listing The Google Play listing: its text (title, short description and full description), its phone screenshots, its store icon and its feature graphic. All of them are made only in pull requests and reviewed there; a release ships what was reviewed and makes nothing of its own. The listing's category, tags, website and contact email are entered in Play Console by the owner, not compiled from this repository; they are recorded in Play Console listing details . The phone screenshots are rendered from the app's own screens on the JVM (Robolectric, through Roborazzi), never captured by hand from a device, so they change only when the screens or the captions do, and every change is reviewed as an image diff in a pull request (STORE-SHOT-001 to STORE-SHOT-015). The store icon and the feature graphic are rendered the same way, the icon from the app's own launcher icon resources and the graphic from the same showcase screens as the shots, and reviewed the same way (STORE-ICON-001 to STORE-ICON-005, STORE-GRAPHIC-001 to STORE-GRAPHIC-007). The text is hand-written, one claim per line, and each claim names the requirements it rests on, so the listing can never promise what the specification does not say (STORE-LIST-001 to STORE-LIST-007). The listing's title is also the app's name on the phone (STORE-LIST-008). The shots Each shot shows a screen as it exists in the app, with the showcase data of STORE-SHOT-006. STORE-SHOT-001 Home: today's reminders and the goals card with goal progress (HOME-002, HOME-006). Light theme. STORE-SHOT-002 The stretch session opened from a reminder, with some of its stretches checked (SESS-001 to SESS-003). Dark theme. STORE-SHOT-003 Daily goals, with goals partway done (GOAL-001, GOAL-003). Light theme. STORE-SHOT-004 The schedule editor on a repeating schedule, showing its interval, minute, window and slot preview (SCHED-011, SCHED-012). Dark theme. STORE-SHOT-005 Weekly trends with the period summary and the current streak (TREND-004 to TREND-006). Light theme. There is no shot of the skipped-days screen. Inputs STORE-SHOT-006 Every shot is rendered from frozen inputs, so the same commit always gives the same pixels: the time is Friday 16 October 2026, 9:40 AM, in America/New_York, read from a fixed clock ( Clock.fixed , SCHED-016) whose zone is also set as the JVM's default time zone; the locale is en-US (Robolectric qualifier and the JVM default), with the 12-hour clock; the device is Robolectric's w411dp-h891dp-xxhdpi (density 3) on a pinned SDK, with native graphics; the colour schemes are the app's fixed light and dark schemes, dynamic colour off; animations are off: each screen is composed straight into its final state, the animator duration scale is 0, and the capture waits until composition is idle; the data comes from one ShowcaseFixture that builds each screen's state directly: the seeded stretch library (LIB-002), three goals partway done today, one set-times schedule and one repeating schedule, and 30 days of completion history. Invariant — The showcase never touches a database or randomness. No Room, no StretchApp , no Random , no system clock: a screen that only takes a ViewModel is rendered through its stateless content composable with state the fixture built. - STORE-SHOT-007 The images are PNGs in fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/ (fastlane supply's layout), named in listing order: 1_home.png , 2_session.png , 3_goals.png , 4_schedule.png , 5_trends.png . Their caption text lives only in docs/store/captions.md , one entry per shot ID (STORE-SHOT-001 to STORE-SHOT-005), which the screenshot test reads. The file's only other entry is the feature graphic's text (STORE-GRAPHIC-003). Layout All sizes are pixels of the final image. STORE-SHOT-010 Each shot is one 1080 x 2340 image: a caption at the top and a framed phone screen below it, cut off by the bottom edge. STORE-SHOT-011 The background is solid #1361A7 on every shot, light and dark: no gradient and nothing else drawn on it. Invariant — A shot's light or dark theme changes only the screen inside the frame, never the background behind it. - STORE-SHOT-012 The caption is left-aligned, 108 px from the top, with 79 px side margins (922 px wide). Headline: white, bold, 90 px, 1.18 line height, at most 3 lines. Supporting line: #CFE1F5, regular, 50 px, 1.35 line height, 22 px below the headline, at most 2 lines. - STORE-SHOT-013 The phone frame's top edge is at y = 650 px on every shot. The frame is centred horizontally and 922 px wide. Its bezel is #0A0A0B, 18 px thick on the top and sides, with no bottom bezel and 79 px radius top corners. The real screen, laid out at the device's natural size (411 x 891 dp), is scaled down to fit inside the bezel. - STORE-SHOT-014 There is no status bar, navigation bar or other device chrome. Invariant — A caption that is too long fails the test instead of shrinking the text or pushing the frame down. Lines are counted as rendered (measured text layout at the caption's width, font and size), not as characters. Store icon and feature graphic Two more images, beside the screenshots in fastlane supply's images folder. Both are rendered on the JVM on the STORE-SHOT-006 device (Robolectric, native graphics, SDK and qualifiers pinned). The store icon is drawn by StoreArtTest with no clock, locale or data involved. The feature graphic is composed by FeatureGraphicTest with all of STORE-SHOT-006's frozen inputs, because it shows two of the app's screens. Store icon STORE-ICON-001 The store icon is fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/icon.png : exactly 512 x 512 px, a 32-bit PNG with an alpha channel (8-bit RGBA, PNG colour type 6). It is a full square: no rounded corners, mask, shadow or margin of its own (Google Play applies its own mask). The file is at most 1024 KB (1,048,576 bytes), Google Play's limit for the store icon. STORE-ICON-002 It is drawn from the app's real adaptive launcher icon: the test inflates @mipmap/ic_launcher and draws its background layer ( @color/ic_launcher_background , #FFFFFF) and then its foreground layer ( @drawable/ic_launcher_foreground ). The monochrome layer is not drawn. Invariant — The store icon is always rendered from the launcher icon and never hand-edited. The test inflates the launcher icon's own resources rather than a copy of their geometry or colours, so any change to the launcher icon changes the rendered store icon and fails the verify (STORE-ICON-004) until the store icon is re-recorded. - STORE-ICON-003 The launcher icon's viewport, its central 72 x 72 dp (the most a launcher's mask can show; the smaller 66 dp safe zone is what no mask clips), fills the image. The layers' 108 x 108 dp canvas is scaled by 512 / 72 px per dp, to 768 x 768 px, and drawn offset by -128 px on both axes, so the outer 18 dp on each side falls outside the image. Feature graphic A headline on the left and two of the app's phone screens on the right, tilted towards each other and running off the bottom edge, drawn like the screenshots' framed phones. All sizes are pixels of the final image. A rotation is in degrees, positive clockwise, about the frame's bottom centre (the middle of its bottom edge, before rotating). STORE-GRAPHIC-001 The feature graphic is fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/featureGraphic.png : exactly 1024 x 500 px, a 24-bit PNG with no alpha channel (8-bit RGB, PNG colour type 2). STORE-GRAPHIC-002 The background is solid #1361A7, the screenshots' colour (STORE-SHOT-011), and runs to every edge: no gradient. On it, in drawing order: the text (STORE-GRAPHIC-003, STORE-GRAPHIC-004), the back phone and then the front phone (STORE-GRAPHIC-005), so the front phone partly covers the back one. Nothing else is drawn: no app icon, app name, logo, badge or device chrome. Invariant — The feature graphic never shows the app icon. Google Play shows the app icon beside the feature graphic and advises against repeating it, so the test draws neither the launcher icon nor the store icon, in any form, anywhere on the graphic. - STORE-GRAPHIC-003 The text is a headline and a supporting line. Their wording lives only in docs/store/captions.md , in its ## STORE-GRAPHIC-003 entry (a Headline: line and a Supporting: line, like the shots' captions, STORE-SHOT-007), which the test reads. Both are claims: each of the two lines ends with one tag, <!-- ID, ID --> , naming the requirements it rests on, and the test fails unless every cited ID is defined by a spec page and not retired (the rule of STORE-LIST-003). The tag is not part of the drawn text. - STORE-GRAPHIC-004 The text block is left-aligned, its left edge at x = 64 px, and 380 px wide. Headline: white (#FFFFFF), Roboto Bold (weight 700), 46 px, 52 px line height, at most 3 lines. Supporting line: #CFE1F5, Roboto Regular (weight 400), 21 px, 29 px line height, 18 px below the headline, at most 2 lines. Each line is its line height, the text centred in it, nothing trimmed (where the font is taller than the line height, as the headline's is, the text engine may keep its full ascent on the first line and descent on the last). The block is centred vertically: its top is at (500 − block height) / 2 px, rounded down, where the block height is the headline's and the supporting line's heights as laid out (measured at the block's width, font and size) plus the 18 px gap. Invariant — Text that does not fit its lines fails the test instead of shrinking or moving. As for the shots' captions (STORE-SHOT-014), lines are counted as rendered (measured text layout at the block's width, font and size), not as characters; nothing shrinks the text, widens the block or moves the phones to make it fit. - STORE-GRAPHIC-005 Two phones, each drawn like a shot's frame (STORE-SHOT-013, STORE-SHOT-014) at a smaller size: a #0A0A0B bezel 9 px thick on the top and sides, no bottom bezel, 36 px radius top corners; the screen inside it has 27 px radius top corners (the frame's radius less the bezel), is laid out at the device's natural size (411 x 891 dp) and is scaled down to fit the bezel's inside width, top-anchored, and is cut off by the frame's bottom edge. There is no status bar, navigation bar or other device chrome. Before rotating: Phone Screen Theme Left Top Width Height Rotation Back The stretch session (STORE-SHOT-002) Dark 720 96 250 447 +6° Front Home (STORE-SHOT-001) Light 520 50 270 485 −4° The heights are the bezel plus the screen's width × 1672 / 886, rounded, so each phone shows the same part of its screen as its shot does (a shot's screen area is 886 x 1672 px). After rotating, each frame's bottom edge lies wholly below the image (y > 500) and its top and sides inside it, so the phones run off the bottom edge only. Each frame casts a drop shadow, drawn under it and rotated with it: black at 35 % opacity (#59000000), offset 18 px down, blur radius 42 px (Android's Paint.setShadowLayer ; a Gaussian sigma of about 25 px). The background, text, bezels and shadows are drawn outside the app theme; only the screens are themed. - STORE-GRAPHIC-006 The fonts are Roboto Bold and Roboto Regular from Roboto 2 ( Roboto-Bold.ttf and Roboto-Regular.ttf , version 2.001047, from the googlefonts/roboto repository), under the Apache License 2.0. The two files and their licence text are committed in app/src/test/resources/store/fonts/ . The test loads those files, never a system font, and fails if either cannot be loaded. - STORE-GRAPHIC-007 The two screens are the app's real composables, rendered the way their shots are: the same stateless content composables with the same ShowcaseFixture state as STORE-SHOT-001 and STORE-SHOT-002, in the shot's fixed theme with dynamic colour off, and with every frozen input of STORE-SHOT-006 (clock, zone, locale, 12-hour clock, device, density, no animations). They change whenever those screens or the fixture change. Invariant — The feature graphic's screens are rendered from the showcase fixture, never pasted in from an image. Nothing drawn on the graphic comes from an image file: the test does not read, crop or scale a committed screenshot or any other image to make it (a verify run reads only the committed feature graphic, to compare). It shares the shots' rendering code rather than a copy of it, so a screen cannot drift from its shot. Writing and checking the two images STORE-ICON-004 Roborazzi writes every image as RGBA, which the feature graphic must not be, so the two tests ( StoreArtTest for the store icon, FeatureGraphicTest for the feature graphic) write and compare the images themselves, through one shared recorder, following the mode the Roborazzi Gradle task sets: ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug writes both files in the formats of STORE-ICON-001 and STORE-GRAPHIC-001, then reads each back and checks its size and colour type; ./gradlew verifyRoborazziDebug (what CI runs) compares each rendered image pixel for pixel with the committed file, with no tolerance, and fails on any difference in size or pixels or on a missing file. On a failure it writes the rendered image to app/build/outputs/roborazzi/ as icon_actual.png or featureGraphic_actual.png , where CI uploads it with the screenshot diffs (STORE-SHOT-008), and leaves the committed file untouched; plain ./gradlew test renders both images and writes and compares nothing. STORE-ICON-005 On every run except a recording, a test reads the committed icon.png and featureGraphic.png and fails unless each exists with exactly the size and PNG colour type of STORE-ICON-001 and STORE-GRAPHIC-001, and unless icon.png is within STORE-ICON-001's 1024 KB limit. The feature graphic has no file size check. Recording and verifying Invariant — A store screenshot is recorded only when a person asks for it, and reaches the default branch only through a pull request whose diff shows the new image. This section applies to the store icon and the feature graphic exactly as to the screenshots; together they are the store images. Invariant — CI only verifies the store images; it never re-records them. No check that runs on a pull request or a release writes a store image. A recording runs only when a person applies the label (STORE-SHOT-009), and its commit reaches the pull request only through that person's own push. STORE-SHOT-008 Every pull request's build ( pr.yml ) only verifies the committed store images ( ./gradlew verifyRoborazziDebug , which fails on any changed or missing screenshot, store icon or feature graphic) and, when it fails, uploads the rendered and diff images as the store-screenshot-diffs artifact. It never records. STORE-SHOT-009 Recording happens in one of two ways, both started by a person: In CI: a person applies the record-store-screenshots label to a pull request from a branch of this repository (never a fork). record-store-screenshots.yml runs ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug on the pull request's head, commits only the store images (the files in the phoneScreenshots folder, icon.png and featureGraphic.png ) as github-actions[bot] , and force-pushes that commit to the side branch store-screenshots/pr-<number> , based on the pull request's head. If no image changed it pushes nothing. Its job summary says which commit to bring in, and it always removes the label afterwards, so the label can be applied again for another recording. Locally: ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug , on Linux with JDK 17 as CI runs. Robolectric draws with its own fonts and renderer, but the host's JDK formats dates and times, and anti-aliasing can differ between operating systems. Invariant — The recording workflow never pushes to the pull request's branch. A push made with the workflow's token starts no pr.yml run, so a person brings the side branch's commit into the pull request with their own push ( git fetch origin store-screenshots/pr-<number> && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD , or a cherry-pick). That push runs pr.yml , which verifies the new images, and the pull request's diff shows them for review. - STORE-SHOT-015 When a pull request from a branch of this repository closes, merged or not, delete-store-screenshots-branch.yml deletes its side branch store-screenshots/pr-<number> (STORE-SHOT-009). The repository's automatic deletion of head branches does not cover it, because the side branch is never a pull request's head. A pull request that never recorded has no side branch, and its absence is not a failure: the run succeeds when the branch does not exist. Any other failure to delete fails the run. The job's token can write contents and nothing else, and it runs for no fork's pull request (a fork's pull request never records, so it has no side branch). Reopening a pull request does not bring its side branch back; applying the label again records again. Listing text Invariant — The listing is never generated at release time. The release run only verifies and packages text and images that were already reviewed in pull requests: nothing in it writes, rewrites or records listing text or screenshots. STORE-LIST-001 The listing text is written by hand in docs/store/listing.md , in three sections, exactly these and in this order: ## Title , ## Short description and ## Full description . Text before ## Title explains the page and is not part of the listing. The title and the short description are one line each. Every non-blank line of the full description is one claim : a paragraph line or a - list item, ending with one tag that lists the requirement IDs it rests on, for example - Set a daily goal for each stretch. <!-- GOAL-001 --> . The title and the short description may carry a tag as well. .github/scripts/store_listing.py compiles the page into fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/title.txt , short_description.txt and full_description.txt (fastlane supply's layout), with the tags removed, the claims' text kept as written, and runs of blank lines collapsed into one paragraph break. The three files are committed with the listing change that produced them; they are never edited by hand. STORE-LIST-002 Every page in docs/spec/ except this folder's README.md (the index, which defines no requirements) starts with a store marker as its first line , followed by a blank line, in exactly one of two forms: <!-- store: headline --> or <!-- store: omit --> . The marker is an HTML comment, so MkDocs renders nothing for it. A headline page describes a feature the listing must mention; an omit page need not be mentioned (its IDs may still be cited). docs.text: The Google Play listing: its text (title, short description and full description), its phone screenshots, its store icon and its feature graphic. All of them are made only in pull requests and reviewed there; a release ships what was reviewed and makes nothing of its own. The listing's category, tags, website and contact email are entered in Play Console by the owner, not compiled from this repository; they are recorded in Play Console listing details . The phone screenshots are rendered from the app's own screens on the JVM (Robolectric, through Roborazzi), never captured by hand from a device, so they change only when the screens or the captions do, and every change is reviewed as an image diff in a pull request (STORE-SHOT-001 to STORE-SHOT-015). The store icon and the feature graphic are rendered the same way, the icon from the app's own launcher icon resources and the graphic from the same showcase screens as the shots, and reviewed the same way (STORE-ICON-001 to STORE-ICON-005, STORE-GRAPHIC-001 to STORE-GRAPHIC-007). The text is hand-written, one claim per line, and each claim names the requirements it rests on, so the listing can never promise what the specification does not say (STORE-LIST-001 to STORE-LIST-007). The listing's title is also the app's name on the phone (STORE-LIST-008).

docs.text: STORE-SHOT-006 Every shot is rendered from frozen inputs, so the same commit always gives the same pixels: the time is Friday 16 October 2026, 9:40 AM, in America/New_York, read from a fixed clock ( Clock.fixed , SCHED-016) whose zone is also set as the JVM's default time zone; the locale is en-US (Robolectric qualifier and the JVM default), with the 12-hour clock; the device is Robolectric's w411dp-h891dp-xxhdpi (density 3) on a pinned SDK, with native graphics; the colour schemes are the app's fixed light and dark schemes, dynamic colour off; animations are off: each screen is composed straight into its final state, the animator duration scale is 0, and the capture waits until composition is idle; the data comes from one ShowcaseFixture that builds each screen's state directly: the seeded stretch library (LIB-002), three goals partway done today, one set-times schedule and one repeating schedule, and 30 days of completion history. STORE-ICON-002 It is drawn from the app's real adaptive launcher icon: the test inflates @mipmap/ic_launcher and draws its background layer ( @color/ic_launcher_background , #FFFFFF) and then its foreground layer ( @drawable/ic_launcher_foreground ). The monochrome layer is not drawn. Invariant — The store icon is always rendered from the launcher icon and never hand-edited. The test inflates the launcher icon's own resources rather than a copy of their geometry or colours, so any change to the launcher icon changes the rendered store icon and fails the verify (STORE-ICON-004) until the store icon is re-recorded. - STORE-ICON-003 The launcher icon's viewport, its central 72 x 72 dp (the most a launcher's mask can show; the smaller 66 dp safe zone is what no mask clips), fills the image. The layers' 108 x 108 dp canvas is scaled by 512 / 72 px per dp, to 768 x 768 px, and drawn offset by -128 px on both axes, so the outer 18 dp on each side falls outside the image.

The tag is not part of the drawn text. - STORE-GRAPHIC-004 The text block is left-aligned, its left edge at x = 64 px, and 380 px wide. Headline: white (#FFFFFF), Roboto Bold (weight 700), 46 px, 52 px line height, at most 3 lines. Supporting line: #CFE1F5, Roboto Regular (weight 400), 21 px, 29 px line height, 18 px below the headline, at most 2 lines. Each line is its line height, the text centred in it, nothing trimmed (where the font is taller than the line height, as the headline's is, the text engine may keep its full ascent on the first line and descent on the last). The block is centred vertically: its top is at (500 − block height) / 2 px, rounded down, where the block height is the headline's and the supporting line's heights as laid out (measured at the block's width, font and size) plus the 18 px gap. Invariant — Text that does not fit its lines fails the test instead of shrinking or moving. As for the shots' captions (STORE-SHOT-014), lines are counted as rendered (measured text layout at the block's width, font and size), not as characters; nothing shrinks the text, widens the block or moves the phones to make it fit. - STORE-GRAPHIC-005 Two phones, each drawn like a shot's frame (STORE-SHOT-013, STORE-SHOT-014) at a smaller size: a #0A0A0B bezel 9 px thick on the top and sides, no bottom bezel, 36 px radius top corners; the screen inside it has 27 px radius top corners (the frame's radius less the bezel), is laid out at the device's natural size (411 x 891 dp) and is scaled down to fit the bezel's inside width, top-anchored, and is cut off by the frame's bottom edge. docs.text: STORE-ICON-004 Roborazzi writes every image as RGBA, which the feature graphic must not be, so the two tests ( StoreArtTest for the store icon, FeatureGraphicTest for the feature graphic) write and compare the images themselves, through one shared recorder, following the mode the Roborazzi Gradle task sets: ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug writes both files in the formats of STORE-ICON-001 and STORE-GRAPHIC-001, then reads each back and checks its size and colour type; ./gradlew verifyRoborazziDebug (what CI runs) compares each rendered image pixel for pixel with the committed file, with no tolerance, and fails on any difference in size or pixels or on a missing file.
