docs.text: Invariant — A store screenshot is recorded only when a person asks for it, and reaches the default branch only through a pull request whose diff shows the new image. This section applies to the store icon and the feature graphic exactly as to the screenshots; together they are the store images. Invariant — CI only verifies the store images; it never re-records them. No check that runs on a pull request or a release writes a store image. A recording runs only when a person applies the label (STORE-SHOT-009), and its commit reaches the pull request only through that person's own push. STORE-SHOT-008 Every pull request's build ( pr.yml ) only verifies the committed store images ( ./gradlew verifyRoborazziDebug , which fails on any changed or missing screenshot, store icon or feature graphic) and, when it fails, uploads the rendered and diff images as the store-screenshot-diffs artifact. It never records. STORE-SHOT-009 Recording happens in one of two ways, both started by a person: In CI: a person applies the record-store-screenshots label to a pull request from a branch of this repository (never a fork). record-store-screenshots.yml runs ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug on the pull request's head, commits only the store images (the files in the phoneScreenshots folder, icon.png and featureGraphic.png ) as github-actions[bot] , and force-pushes that commit to the side branch store-screenshots/pr-<number> , based on the pull request's head. If no image changed it pushes nothing. Its job summary says which commit to bring in, and it always removes the label afterwards, so the label can be applied again for another recording. Locally: ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug , on Linux with JDK 17 as CI runs. Robolectric draws with its own fonts and renderer, but the host's JDK formats dates and times, and anti-aliasing can differ between operating systems. Invariant — The recording workflow never pushes to the pull request's branch. A push made with the workflow's token starts no pr.yml run, so a person brings the side branch's commit into the pull request with their own push ( git fetch origin store-screenshots/pr-<number> && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD , or a cherry-pick). That push runs pr.yml , which verifies the new images, and the pull request's diff shows them for review. - STORE-SHOT-015 When a pull request from a branch of this repository closes, merged or not, delete-store-screenshots-branch.yml deletes its side branch store-screenshots/pr-<number> (STORE-SHOT-009). The repository's automatic deletion of head branches does not cover it, because the side branch is never a pull request's head. A pull request that never recorded has no side branch, and its absence is not a failure: the run succeeds when the branch does not exist. Any other failure to delete fails the run. The job's token can write contents and nothing else, and it runs for no fork's pull request (a fork's pull request never records, so it has no side branch). Reopening a pull request does not bring its side branch back; applying the label again records again.

docs.text: Trends How well the daily goals (goals.md) were kept, by week or month, with a drill-down into one day. Everything here is derived from the goal history (GOAL-008), the completion log (SESS-004) and the skipped dates (SKIP-007); nothing is stored. TREND-001 A day is judged by the goals in force that day (GOAL-008), not by today's goals. A goal changed on the 5th from 3 to 1 a day asks for 3 on the 4th and 1 on the 5th; a goal removed on the 7th no longer counts from the 7th but still counts before it. Invariant — Changing or removing a goal never changes a past day's score. Past days are scored from the goal rows whose range covers them, which an edit closes rather than overwrites (GOAL-009). - TREND-002 A day's score is the sum, over the goals in force that day, of min(completions of that goal's stretch that day, its target), divided by the sum of the targets. Completions count by local calendar day as in GOAL-003. Example: hamstring 3 a day and calf 2 a day; 4 hamstring and 1 calf gives (3 + 1) / 5 = 80%. A day is all goals met when every goal in force reached its target (score 100%). Invariant — Extra completions never lift a score. Completions beyond a goal's target, and completions of stretches without a goal that day, add nothing: a day never exceeds 100%, and over-doing one goal never makes up for another. - TREND-003 A day with no goals in force, a skipped day (SKIP-001, SKIP-002) and a day after today have no score . They are shown as gaps and left out of every average, count and streak. Invariant — A gap is never 0%. A day without a score is never drawn as a 0% bar or averaged in as 0; a scored day with nothing done is 0% and is drawn differently from a gap. - TREND-004 The Trends screen has a Week / Month toggle (Week first) and previous / next buttons that move one period at a time. A week runs Monday to Sunday ; a month runs from the 1st to its last day. The period's title reads like "Oct 5 – 11, 2026" or "October 2026". Next is disabled once the period contains today (no browsing into the future); previous is disabled once the period starts on or before the first day any goal was in force. Switching between week and month shows the period containing today when today is in view, otherwise the period containing the first day shown. A bar chart shows one bar per day of the period, its height the day's score on a 0–100% axis; all-met days are drawn in the full accent colour, partial days lighter, gaps as a dashed outline at the baseline, and today is underlined. - TREND-005 Above the chart, a summary for the shown period: the average score over the scored days in it (and how many days that is; "–" when none), and the number of days with all goals met . - TREND-006 The summary also shows the current streak : the number of consecutive all-goals-met days ending today or yesterday, counted back through all history (not only the shown period). Today adds to the streak once it is met but never breaks it, because the day is not over. Gaps (TREND-003) are passed over: a skipped day or a day without goals neither adds to nor breaks a streak. The first earlier scored day that was not fully met ends it. - TREND-007 Tapping a day's bar (today or earlier) opens the day detail screen: the day's score (or why it has none), each goal in force that day with done / target and a progress bar, and every completion logged that day with its time, in time order (including stretches without a goal). - TREND-008 The day detail screen also shows the score through the day as a step chart: x is the time of day from 0:00 to 24:00, y is 0–100%. It starts at 0% at midnight and steps up at the time of each completion that counts towards a goal (TREND-002), staying level in between; completions saved together (one session save, SESS-003) make one step. The line runs to the current time for today and to midnight for past days. A day without goals in force has no chart. If the clocks go back during the night, time of day never runs backwards on the chart. - TREND-009 The Trends screen is reached from a labelled "Trends" item in the home screen's overflow menu (HOME-004) and from a "Trends" button on the home goals card while goals exist (HOME-006). - TREND-010 Accessibility: each day's bar is its own accessible element whose content description gives the date and the score, done / target and "all goals met" (or "skipped", "no goals", "not yet"), and announces tapping as "Show day". The step chart has one content description listing each step's time and score. Charts are drawn with Compose Canvas ; no chart library is used. Build checklist [x] TrendMath (goals in force, daily score, per-day counts, week/month periods, summary, streak, intraday series) is pure and unit tested (TREND-001..006, TREND-008). [x] Scores are null for gaps, and the average uses only non-null scores (TREND-003 invariant). [x] Credited completions are min(done, target) per goal (TREND-002 invariant). [x] Weeks start Monday via TemporalAdjusters.previousOrSame(MONDAY) , independent of locale (TREND-004). [x] The streak is computed over all days since the first goal, not the shown period (TREND-006). [x] Each bar is a separate composable with clearAndSetSemantics { contentDescription } and a labelled click (TREND-010). [x] Only completions since the first goal day are read for the trends screen (earlier ones can never score). [ ] Compose UI test of the chart semantics (needs an emulator in CI). [x] Store listing reviewed: every claim in docs/store/listing.md that cites this page is still true, and at least one does ( store: headline ; STORE-LIST-003, STORE-LIST-004).

docs.text: Widgets A home screen widget shows today's goals at a glance. The segmented ring is the first widget; the mat-bar and goal-list widgets are later alternatives. Segmented ring WIDGET-001 The widget is 2×2 cells by default and resizable in both directions. It is drawn square, as large as the smaller side allows, centred in its cell area. It has no widget background: only the disc (WIDGET-005), the ring and the centre are drawn. WIDGET-002 The ring has one arc per current goal (GOAL-008), in goals-screen order (GOAL-002: by stretch name, ignoring case, ties by id), clockwise from 12 o'clock. The arcs share the ring equally with a gap of 8° between neighbours; one goal is a full ring with no gap. Arc ends are round, and the 8° is the visible gap between the round ends. Each arc is a track in the track colour with the filled part drawn over it. WIDGET-003 Each arc fills clockwise from its start by that goal's progress / count (GOAL-003), capped at full: 4 of 3 is a full arc. The fill is continuous (2 of 3 is two thirds of the arc), and in-progress and met arcs use the same colour. WIDGET-004 The centre shows the launcher icon's side-bend figure on its mat and, under it, today's count as " done / total ": total is the sum of the current goals' counts and done the sum of each goal's progress capped at its count (so 4 of 3 adds 3). Once every goal is met, the count is replaced by a plain check mark in the text colour, with no circle or badge. WIDGET-005 Behind the ring is a disc in the disc colour at 55% opacity, reaching the ring's inner edge, so the widget reads on black and on light wallpapers. WIDGET-006 States: Nothing done yet (at least one goal, done = 0): the figure is dimmed and the arcs show only their track; the count reads "0/ total ". No goals set : the ring is a dotted track (round dots in the track colour, no arcs), the figure is dimmed and centred, and there is no count and no check mark. Otherwise the figure is drawn in the arc colour. "Dimmed" means the figure (body and head) is drawn in the text colour at 40% opacity; the mat keeps its colour. - WIDGET-007 Tapping the widget opens the app on its home screen (HOME-001): any screen open above home is closed. Colour WIDGET-008 The widget follows the system light/dark mode. Where the phone supports dynamic colour (Android 12 and later, the same test as the app's theme) it uses the wallpaper colours, with the roles Material 3's dynamic schemes use: Part Role Light Dark Arcs and figure primary system_accent1_600 system_accent1_200 Disc (at 55%) surface system_neutral1_10 system_neutral1_900 Text and check mark onSurface system_neutral1_900 system_neutral1_100 Empty track onSurface at 14% (light) / 18% (dark) Mat outline system_neutral2_500 system_neutral2_400 Without dynamic colour it uses the mockup's fixed values: Part Light Dark Arcs and figure #1361A7 #3D86D1 Disc (at 55%) white #121212 Text and check mark #1C1B1F #F5F5F5 Empty track black at 14% white at 18% Mat #818589 #818589 Invariant — The fixed mockup colours are used only when dynamic colour is unavailable. The choice between dynamic and fixed is made in one place, by the same Android-version test as the app's theme; no part of the widget mixes the two. Both the light and the dark drawing are produced at every redraw and the launcher shows the one for the current mode, so switching between light and dark needs no redraw. A change of wallpaper colours shows at the next redraw (WIDGET-010). Data and refresh WIDGET-009 The widget's goals and progress come from the same calculation as the goals screen ( GoalMath.goalRows , GOAL-002/003): current goals only (GOAL-008), with progress counted from the completion log over today's local calendar day. Invariant — Progress is derived from the completion log, never stored (GOAL-004). The widget keeps no counter and no copy of progress between redraws; each redraw reads the log. Invariant — Only today's completions count. Each redraw counts completions from local midnight today to the next local midnight ( GoalMath.dayBounds ), never a rolling 24 hours or a day fixed when the widget was added. - WIDGET-010 The widget redraws: - after every logged completion (SESS-003); - after every goal add, change or removal (GOAL-009), and after a stretch is renamed or deleted (which changes the arcs' order or removes a goal, LIB-005); - at local midnight, through an alarm set for the start of the next local day at each redraw; - when it is added or resized, when the app starts, after a reboot, a time or time-zone change, or an app update. Invariant — The widget never shows a number the app would not. Every write that can change today's goals or progress (completions, goals, stretches) is followed by a redraw, made from the repository, not from a screen, so no screen can forget it; and the midnight alarm is re-armed at every redraw, so a new day always starts at 0. Build checklist [x] GoalRing.model is pure and unit tested for 0, 1, 3 and 8 goals; none, partly and all met; progress above the count; and no goals (WIDGET-002 … WIDGET-006). [x] GoalRing.fromLog builds the ring from GoalMath.goalRows , the goals screen's calculation, and drops stretches without a goal (WIDGET-009). [x] GoalRing.nextRedrawAt is the next local midnight, including across a daylight-saving change (WIDGET-010). [x] WidgetPalette.select returns the fixed mockup values only when dynamic colour is unavailable, and its fixed values match WIDGET-008 (unit tested). [x] The renderer draws round arc ends inside each arc's share, so the visible gap is 8° (WIDGET-002). [x] StretchRepository requests a redraw after logCompletions , setGoal , removeGoal , saveStretch and deleteStretch (WIDGET-010 invariant). [x] The midnight alarm is re-armed at every redraw and cancelled when the last widget is removed (WIDGET-010). [x] Tapping opens home with any screen above it closed (WIDGET-007). [ ] On a device: light and dark, dynamic colour on and off, resize, tap, and the midnight reset (human-only issue). [x] Store listing reviewed: every claim in docs/store/listing.md that cites this page is still true, and at least one does ( store: headline ; STORE-LIST-003, STORE-LIST-004).

docs.text: Store screenshot captions The caption on each Google Play phone screenshot, one entry per shot ID of the store listing specification , and last the text of the feature graphic. This file is the only place the text lives: the screenshot and feature graphic tests read it, and a caption that does not fit (at most 3 headline lines and 2 supporting lines, as rendered) fails that test (STORE-SHOT-012, STORE-SHOT-014, STORE-GRAPHIC-004). Each entry is a ## heading with the shot ID, then a Headline: line and a Supporting: line. Changing a caption changes its image, which is then re-recorded in the same pull request (the record-store-screenshots label, or ./gradlew recordRoborazziDebug locally; STORE-SHOT-009). The feature graphic's entry, STORE-GRAPHIC-003 , is a pair of claims: each of its two lines ends with the requirement IDs it rests on as an HTML comment, e.g. <!-- SCHED-001 --> , as in the listing text . The comment is not drawn; the test fails if a line has none or cites an ID the specification does not define or has retired (STORE-GRAPHIC-003). Only claim what the cited requirements say. How to write it: Keep exactly the three sections below, in this order. Everything above ## Title (this explanation) is not part of the listing. The title (at most 30 characters) and the short description (at most 80) are one line each. The title is also the app's name on the phone: the app_name string in app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml must say exactly the same, and a test fails when they differ ( STORE-LIST-008 ). Change both together. Every line of the full description (at most 4,000 characters) is one claim, written as plain text and ending with the requirement IDs it rests on as an HTML comment, e.g. <!-- GOAL-001, HOME-006 --> . The comment does not show on this page or in the listing; view the page's source to see the IDs. Only claim what the cited requirements say. Every spec page marked <!-- store: headline --> needs at least one claim citing one of its IDs. After editing, run python3 .github/scripts/store_listing.py and commit the three files it writes with this page.
